To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated 20μm-pitch micro-via arrays at <10μm via-diameter in ultra-thin (10μm) ZS100 dry-film polymer for 2.5/3D interposer applications.

we have demonstrated 8-10 μm diameter via arrays at 20 μm pitch in 10 μm thick polymer dielectric dry films on glass and organic interposer substrates by excimer laser direct-write, followed by electroless and electrolysis plating to form fully filled micro-vias.
the use of excimer laser ablations in ultra-thin polymer dielectric layers enables high density micro-via formation for low-cost and scalable RDL for 2.5-D/3D interposery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, high-density and low cost redistribution layer (RDL) technology for 2.5/3D interposer applications.
the development of a novel 20μm micro-via technology for high-density and low cost 3D integration of glass and organic interconnect substrates.
the development of a new class of high-performance, low-cost and low-CTE interposers for 2.5 and 3D IC packaging applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

20μm micro-vias in ultra-thin polymer dielectrics have been achieved using excimer laser via formation, and electroless/electrolytic plating to form fully filled vias, and that this process is scalable to large panels.
this paper demonstrates the first 20μm micro-via pitch on ultra-thin dielectrics for high-density and low cost 3D packaging on glass interposer substrates.

this work demonstrates the first 20um pitch micro-vias in ultra-thin polymer dielectrics by laser ablation, which are scalable to large panels and suitable for high density and low-cost 3D integration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 20μm-pitch micro-vias were successfully formed by excimer laser via patterning and SAP processes.
we have successfully demonstrated the feasibility of using excimer laser direct-write for the formation of micro-vias at high densities and low pitches in thin dielectrics on large panels.
the use of dry-film polymer laminates with excimer laser ablated vias and semi-additive metallization is a viable approach for low-cost and large panel based 2.5/3D interposer technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 20μm via pitch is a key metric for the next generation of high density interposer technologies.

the combination of excimer laser via ablation and electroless and electrolytically plated copper metallization can be used for high density RDL on glass and organic interposer substrates, and is scalable to large panels.
the use of excimer laser ablated micro-vias in ultra-thin polymer dielectric films is a promising approach to achieve high density and low cost RDL on panel-based glass interposers.
